description_en: The monument is situated on the edge of a hill in the locality of Chipur. In close proximity, around 500 meters to the west, there is a water reservoir and a pavilion known as Chipur Hati Bhātko Nāulo (DDL0280). The carvings on both monuments share similar stylistic features. Adjacent to the pavilion in the northwest direction is a rectangular house-like structure constructed with carved stones. Within and around this building, stone memorial pillars (khamba) and architectural pillars, potentially originating from a pavilion, are displayed.The pavilion is oriented towards the north, east, south, and west corners. It is constructed on a stone platform, with eight pillars supporting a corbelled dome. In 2011, Prayag Raj Sharma reported that the roof of thebhaithaka(pavilion) had completely collapsed (Sharma 2012, p. 323). However, the roof was rebuilt prior to the site's survey in 2015. According to local informants, the structure is known as Pañca Bhāiyya Bhaiṭak (Five Brothers Pavilion). This name may refer to the Pāṇḍava Brothers from Hindu mythology. Additionally, the pillars are adorned with relief carvings depicting five anthropomorphic figures, possibly warriors. The rest of the decorative motifs mainly consist of stylized variations of thekalaśamotif.Determining the exact antiquity of the monument is challenging. According to D. R. Sharma, local accounts mention that the nearby Chipur Hati Bhātko Nāulo (DDL0280) was built by a person named Hati Bhāt "during the time of Nāga Malla of Doti state in the 14th century." It is also said that Hati Bhāt's wife constructed another reservoir in the vicinity, but its location is unknown (Sharma 2012, p. 321-323). Considering the stylistic similarity between the carvings on this monument and those on the Hati Bhātko Nāulo, it is reasonable to assume that they were constructed around the same period. Furthermore, the 14th and 15th centuries were characterized by significant architectural activity in the region, as evidenced by the numerous monuments erected during that time in the Dadeldhura and Baitadi districts.
monument_assessment: Good (very few light surface damages, renovated or repaired), Rebuilt, Restored
references: REFERENCES Sharma, Dilli Raj. 2012. Heritage of Western Nepal. Art and Architecture . Kathmandu: Centre for Nepal and Asian Studies.
